purpose: Per-fuel operational constants required by SS3.9's fuel record and consumed by SS3.3's ignition/extinction gates, SS3.4's soot ledger, and SS3.5's radiative budget. Companion to the methane gas_thermochemistry record; see FIRE_SMOKE_DESIGN.md SS12 item 6 (r51 bring-up rule).

related_findings_not_in_this_record.T_CFT_methane: FDS Source/data.f90 LOOKUP_CRITICAL_FLAME_TEMPERATURE gives methane 1507 C = 1780 K, against the generic ~1700 K pinned in the SS12 item-7 transport record. If the transport record is ever made per-fuel, methane's own value is 1780 K.
related_findings_not_in_this_record.lower_oxygen_limit_methane: FDS data.f90 LOOKUP_LOWER_OXYGEN_LIMIT methane = 0.139 volume fraction

T_AIT.applicability: spontaneous-ignition route of SS3.3's two-route gate, 1 atm, air

provenance.alternative: Robinson & Smith, J. Hazardous Materials 8(3):199-203 (1984), 873 K - PAYWALLED, abstract open via OSTI
provenance.citation: Zabetakis, 'Flammability Characteristics of Combustible Gases and Vapors', US Bureau of Mines Bulletin 627 (1965)
provenance.locator: Table 4 p.25 (999 F = 810.4 K, methane in air); Table A-1 gives 540 C = 813.2 K
provenance.modelling_practice: FDS User's Guide example uses 540 C; FDS UMD Line Burner methane input uses 600 C citing SFPE Table 2-8.2

uncertainty.note: Two defensible camps. Handbook consensus 810-813 K; Robinson & Smith 1984 argue the accepted value was theoretically rather than experimentally derived and that no firm experimental value lies below 873 K (600 C). Apparatus-dependent engineering quantity, not a thermodynamic constant: Bulletin 627 predates ASTM E659 and used Setchkin 1-L and 200-cc Pyrex flasks, with the bulletin itself warning that flask shape and size matter.

T_ox.applicability: soot oxidation activation threshold, SS3.4; fuel-independent to first order

provenance.citation: Kent & Wagner, Combust. Sci. Technol. 41(5-6):245-269 (1984): flames emit smoke when soot temperature in the oxidation zone falls below about 1300 K, set by radiative loss from the soot; Glassman, 22nd Symp. (Int.) Combust. (1988): particle burnout ceases at about 1300 K

uncertainty.note: Fuel-independent model closure with a solid empirical basis, not a per-fuel measurement. Basis is empirical burnout quench (kinetics plus radiative cooling), NOT Nagle-Strickland-Constable kinetics alone: NSC was fitted over 1273-2273 K so 1300 K sits at the bottom edge of its calibration, its rate peaks near 1900-2000 K and then declines, and it assumes O2 is the oxidant, underestimating burnout in fuel-rich regions where OH dominates.

T_pilot.applicability: piloted route of SS3.3's ignition gate; numerical closure, applies to the resolved-T field near the pilot mask

provenance.structural_requirement: must lie strictly below T_AIT for the two-route gate to be meaningful; 600 K < 810 K holds

uncertainty.note: MODEL GATE CONSTANT, not a measured per-fuel property - see r52. There is no measured piloted-ignition temperature for a GASEOUS fuel: piloted ignition of a gas is governed by flammability limits and pilot energy, not a bulk temperature threshold. The ~600 K figure that circulates in fire texts is the piloted-ignition SURFACE temperature of SOLIDS (wood, paper), a different quantity that must not be read as a methane property. Corroboration that this class of parameter is numerical: FDS's analogue AUTO_IGNITION_TEMPERATURE defaults to a value that disables the gate, and its User's Guide states the value 'may need to be lowered for cases where the grid size is greater than 10 cm' - a parameter retuned with grid resolution is a closure, not a property.

chi_r.applicability: SS3.5's global radiative budget target beta = chi_r*Qdot_tot/Sum(e*V), and the SS3.8 integrated-radiative-fraction gate

provenance.citation: Beyler, 'Fire Hazard Calculations for Large Open Hydrocarbon Fires', SFPE Handbook 5th ed. Table 66.14 (2016)
provenance.locator: quoted verbatim in FDS Source/data.f90 LOOKUP_CHI_R: CASE('METHANE') ; CHI_R = 0.20_EB
provenance.measured_spread_source: Hostikka, McGrattan & Hamins, IAFSS FSS-7:383-394 (2002), via the 30 open FDS Hamins_Gas_Burners input files

uncertainty.note: CONFIGURATION- AND SCALE-DEPENDENT, not a fuel constant - see r52. FDS states it directly: 'There is no single value of radiative fraction for a given fuel.' The 0.20 default applies to large open hydrocarbon fires. Measured spread: 0.07-0.28 (mean ~0.155) across NIST 0.10/0.38/1.0 m methane burners at 2-200 kW; 0.181 for buoyant turbulent methane (Markstein); 0.14 for 35 m Montoir LNG (large-fire re-absorption). A case record MAY override this for its configuration.

rho_soot.policy: REFERENCED, NOT DUPLICATED. The optics record's density is identity-bearing (hashed with the kappa table so a density change changes the record ID); a second independently-editable copy of a quantity that scales radiance is exactly the drift the pin exists to prevent. The fuel record cites the optics record ID rather than restating the number as its own datum.
rho_soot.provenance_via_optics_record: Bond & Bergstrom 2006 SS9.2 p.58 (measured range 1.7-1.9 g/cm3)

provenance.citation: Koylu, Sivathanu & Faeth, 'Carbon Monoxide and Soot Emissions from Buoyant Turbulent Diffusion Flames', IAFSS Fire Safety Science FSS-3:625-636 (1991), Table 3
provenance.locator: Table 3 (methane eta_s = 0.00; acetylene 0.19, ethylene 0.018, propane 0.012 for scale)
provenance.sanity_check: peak soot volume fraction 0.47 ppm in an atmospheric CH4/air laminar coflow diffusion flame (Smooke et al., Combust. Flame 117:117-139 (1999), PAYWALLED; quoted with conditions in Zhang, Univ. Toronto PhD thesis 2009 SS4.3.1, open) - sub-ppm confirms 'very low sooting'

uncertainty.note: Methane is effectively non-sooting. Koylu/Sivathanu/Faeth report the soot generation factor eta_s = 0.00 for methane and state the flames 'emitted no soot for present test conditions' (50 and 234 mm burners, 2.3-23.8 kW, long-residence-time overfire sampling). UNIT CAVEAT: their eta_s is per unit fuel CARBON burned, so y_s = 0.749*eta_s for CH4 - zero either way. FDS ships NO per-fuel soot yield (REAC default 0 kg/kg); its methane validation inputs use SOOT_YIELD=0.01 as a MODELLING CONVENTION with no cited measurement - do not record 0.01 as measured.

visual_consequence_flagged: With y_s = 0 measured, a predictive methane flame produces essentially no soot and therefore almost no thermal continuum in the visible - physically correct (methane burns blue) but it means methane is an excellent SOLVER bring-up fuel and a poor VISUAL one until the SS4.4 chem channels are enabled, which is deferred per SS12 item 1.
